arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Franklin Taylor Rouse argued Congress created the TVA as a corporation that can sue and be sued.
He cited the TVA Act, which states the corporation may sue and be sued in its corporate name.
Ms. O'Connell Adams argued the Court recognized in Burr that such clauses need not waive immunity for everything.
She noted Burr described categories of claims that might not be allowed despite a broad waiver.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests the scope of a sovereign immunity waiver. The Tennessee Valley Authority Act allows the agency to sue and be sued. the sides that brought the case claim this waives immunity for all agency conduct. The agency claims the waiver covers only specific activities. The Court must define the boundary of this waiver.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This dispute defines the scope of sovereign immunity waivers. It determines when citizens can sue federal agencies. It clarifies the legal boundary between public and private agency functions.
